title: A/R Detail lists the five buckets in fixed order and rows by name
custom_preconds:
Setup file (for Claude sessions; a tester does not need it)

Preconditions

  • Scenario: Your customers owe you money in every aging bucket, and one bucket holds invoices from two customers.
  • You are an Admin user (the "Admin" role) working at {Location-A}, your current location.
    For example: {Location-A} is Staging Heavy Duty - 9919.
  • The report has open documents in all five aging buckets on today's date.
  • In the "1-30 days past due" bucket, {Customer-A} has one open invoice, {Invoice-A}, and {Customer-B} has two, {Invoice-B} and {Invoice-C}. {Customer-B}'s name comes first alphabetically, and {Invoice-B}'s number is smaller than {Invoice-C}'s but has fewer digits.
    For example: {Customer-A} is ZZAUTOTEST S1-08 Baker and {Customer-B} is ZZAUTOTEST S1-08 Abbott; {Invoice-B} is S1-99 and {Invoice-C} is S1-100 (the app assigns the real numbers).
  • Starting screen: A/R Detail (Reports, then "A/R Aging Detail" under ACCOUNTS RECEIVABLE in the left menu) is open in a desktop browser window 1440 px wide, as opened from the Reports menu.
  • If any record above is missing, mark this test Blocked: "setup not done".
custom_steps:
1. Read the bucket rows from top to bottom without expanding anything.
  2. Look at the header of the "Customer Full Name" column.
  3. Click the chevron of the "1-30 days past due" bucket to expand it.
custom_expected:
Expected results

  • Step 1: the buckets read, in this order: "91 or more days past due", "61-90 days past due", "31-60 days past due", "1-30 days past due", "Current".
  • Step 2: "Customer Full Name" is marked as the sorted column (a small arrow beside its heading).
  • Step 3: the bucket opens and shows its rows: {Customer-B}'s two invoices come first, {Invoice-B} above {Invoice-C} (smaller number first, counted as a number), then {Customer-A}'s {Invoice-A}.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "A/R and A/P Report Sorting, Export and Location Filter", Confluence 947650561, version 9 (23 Oct 2026, Chris Ward), read 26 Oct 2026 · Epic SV-11315, story SV-11531 (Story 1, Reports open in QuickBooks name order), story SV-11532 (Story 2, Sort by clicking any column header)

  • S1-R5: “A/R Detail and A/P Detail keep their aging buckets in this fixed order: "91 or more days past due", "61-90 days past due", "31-60 days past due", "1-30 days past due", "Current". Inside each bucket, rows open in customer or vendor name order (S1-R2 to S1-R4), ties by document number (S2-R4).”
  • S1-R7: “The column the report opened on is marked as sorted: the name column on the Summaries and Detail reports, the Date column on Collection and Unpaid Invoices.”
  • S2-R4: “ID and No. sort by number value: S1-99 before S1-100 before S1-101. The first click puts the smallest number first and the second click the largest first. The same number-aware order breaks ties in every sort, always smallest document number first: reversing a sort reverses the sorted column only, so tied rows keep that order in both directions. A date column compares the day only, never the time of day, so two rows on the same date are a tie.”

The build is not yet available to check this case against.

Design canvas "A/R and A/P Report Sorting" (https://claude.ai/artifact/BRYCdjKwGRSgGPC9xxkgF4), read 22 Oct 2026: page 1 "Opening order and header sorting" (board Main.dc.html). The design's own words:

  • "Buckets stay in fixed order; rows inside each bucket go by vendor name (was most overdue first). S1-R5, S2-R4, S2-R5." (caption of "A/P Aging Detail opens by vendor name")
  • "Customer name order the way QuickBooks sorts ("10 Trucking" before "2 Trucking"), marked on the Customer header. S1-R1, S1-R2, S1-R4, S1-R7, S1-R8." (caption of "A/R Aging Summary opens A to Z")
  • "Inside a bucket, rows open most overdue first. No sortable headers." (caption of "A/P Aging Detail as it opens today")
